_comment: Voice quality gate definition (plans/voice-quality.md stage 7). Read by tools/voice-gate.
Frozen inputs: 'shim', corpus, receiver, analysis, and every profile field except 'gates' and 'description'.

shim (version 2, since baseline 2.9-slot): the impairment shim draws its random streams (loss, burst state and drop, jitter, reorder) once per 20 ms send slot, not once per packet. The slot of a packet is its RTP timestamp offset (48 kHz media time from the first captured sample) divided by 960. Each stream advances through every slot up to the packet's slot, so a slot without a packet (DTX, a closed gate) consumes its draws, and a sender that sends one packet more or less meets the same network in every later slot. The streams stay independent of each other. Version 1 (baseline 2.9) drew per packet. tools/voice-gate/src/shim.rs.

extra_seeds: the profile also runs with each extra seed as <name>@<seed>, without gates. The harness adds the median over the seed and the extra seeds of latency_clip_growth_ms, mos and bottleneck_delay_mean_ms as <metric>_median. home-wifi, mobile and bad gate in-clip growth on latency_clip_growth_ms_median: one seed's value spreads over more than the limit (TESTING.md, voice quality gate, seeds).
A change to a frozen input changes inputs_fingerprint; the harness then refuses to compare with the baseline.
Gates may change. 'enforced': false prints a failing gate but does not fail the run.
Times are seconds of sender audio from the run start. Delays and stalls are ms.

conceal_per_lost (stage 3b): the denominator counts a lost packet only when NetEQ could conceal it: not a lost Opus DTX frame, and not a loss at the head of a talk spurt before any packet of that spurt was delivered (NetEQ has played nothing of the spurt; it starts with the next packet). TESTING.md, voice quality gate.

conceal_per_lost is informational since stage 3b. One concealment per lost frame was the invariant of the old jitter buffer. NetEQ's expand for one lost frame is often shorter than a frame (merge), and a loss inside a stall shares one expand with it, so the ratio sits under 1 also when the total concealment is unchanged. The harm the gate was for, delay that builds up, is enforced by latency_clip_growth_ms and the drift gate.

recovery_s (stage 3b): on the receiver's NetEQ buffer level (packet buffer, sync buffer and output ring, sampled at every 10 ms pull, mean per analysis hop over the pulls that played decoded audio): back within recovery_tolerance_ms of the median level of the 10 s before the event, and held for recovery_hold_ms. recovery_e2e_s is the earlier definition on the cross-correlated mouth-to-ear delay. TESTING.md, talk-spurt gate.

profiles.description: Clean link (20 ms, 2 ms jitter) with one 5 s burst at 20 s: 60 ms jitter, 10 % loss, a 300 ms stall at its start.

profiles.name: drift
profiles.description: Clean link (20 ms, 2 ms jitter), sender clock +100 ppm fast, 10 minutes. Push-to-talk sender, so the stream has no pauses that reset the playout buffer. RNNoise off on the sender: it costs 5 ms per frame in this build and would make this profile alone take 3 minutes; the profile measures the receive clock path.

gates.note: stage 3 gate: zero drift over 10 minutes
stage 5: MOS drops at most 0.1 against stage 4 (4.25)

profiles.name: outage

gates.note: stage 1.7: back to the pre-outage delay within 5 s; since stage 3b on the NetEQ buffer level, which has no point while the outage plays concealment
stage 1.7 before stage 3b: on the cross-correlated mouth-to-ear delay
stage 5: MOS drops at most 0.1 against stage 4 (2.98)
